evidence.title: Right to Information Act
evidence.key_figure: CIC lists the Right to Information Act, 2005 as the governing statute.

analysis:
The 2004 Congress manifesto said the Right to Information Act at the Centre would be made more progressive, meaningful and useful to the public. It did not set a deadline for the change.

The Right to Information Act, 2005 replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002. It set time limits for public authorities to respond, created a two-tier appeal system and provided penalties for delay. The Act received presidential assent in June 2005 and came into force in October 2005.

The manifesto's target was met by the 2005 Act. The entry is scored against the stated target rather than a date because no deadline was given.
notes: The manifesto release date is not shown on the archive page; 2004-03-01 is used as an approximate date. No deadline was stated for this promise.
